what_happened.line: DEP is expected to require Woodlands move kayak racks out of the Zone One wellhead protection area; the board agreed to wait for DEP's official letter before replying further.
The board agreed its message to Woodlands should be that the racks need to move immediately, not on an extended timeline.
The superintendent reported the Rolling Acres water main replacement is nearly complete and on schedule, and the board backed continued work on a multi-year capital plan for main replacement.
The district's hydrogeologist was given the go-ahead to proceed with the next design step for PFAS testing near Keyes, which will require a future warrant article to fund.
The board also discussed eventual replacement of the district's aging excavation equipment, which would likely need its own warrant article.

why_it_matters: Zone One is the town's wellhead protection area for drinking water, so the kayak-rack dispute touches the safeguards around the water supply.
Any response to PFAS testing at Keyes, and any equipment replacement, would come to residents as a future warrant article -- a vote at town meeting -- rather than being decided by the board alone.
A multi-year capital plan for water main replacement could shape future water rates and the district's borrowing or budget requests.
